title: Shadow Star☆
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: Twelve-year-old Shiina Tamai befriends Hoshimaru, a star-shaped creature she finds on the seabed near her grandparents' home, and learns it is a shadow dragon with great power. Other children have dragons too, and some use them for destructive ends; a group of misanthropic teens aims to end the world, while government agencies close in (AniList; ANN review of early chapters; Grimoire of Horror review).
life_message: Power in the hands of hurt children magnifies the cruelty around them; the story questions whether humanity deserves to continue.

content.note: Gore, body horror, deaths of children (AniList Gore, Body Horror; MU Child/ren Death); reviewer calls the violence 'cruel for the sake of it'.
Cosmic horror, apocalypse, random tragedies (AniList Cosmic Horror; MU Apocalypse; Grimoire review).
Sexual abuse and rape involving young characters listed by AniList (spoiler) and MU; not described in reviews opened, so capped (to verify).
Bullying and mentally damaged children driving rampages (AniList/MU Bullying; Grimoire review).

dominant: Nihilism and misanthropy explored; existential dread; abuse of power by children

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Children answer bullying with dragon violence, shown as destructive (Grimoire review).

Order vs freedom.evidence: Children act outside adult control; agencies fail to contain them (ANN review).

Civic vs kin.evidence: Shiina's ties to her father and friend Akira versus world-ending plans (ANN).

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Child cast set against adult institutions (AniList Primarily Child Cast).

Tradition vs secular-rational.evidence: Science-fiction and philosophy framing, not religious (AniList Philosophy, Sci-Fi).

folkways.japan: School bullying and the isolation of children in late-1990s Japan shape the story; these are presented as social background, not a lesson.

delivery.evidence: Grimoire of Horror criticizes the author's 'lack of subtlety when introducing the most controversial topics' (one source; to verify).

personified.ideology: Humanity is not worth saving and should be ended

delivery.note: The misanthropic view is voiced by hurt teens whose backgrounds make it understandable, while Shiina resists it.

winners_losers: Shiina keeps a hopeful bond with Hoshimaru against teens who want to end the world; the series gives their despair real weight and offers no easy victory.
to_verify: Sexual abuse and rape content (AniList spoiler tag, MU) not confirmed by a review; score may be understated.
